title: After update to 1.66, docker containers cannot access Tailscale IPs
body:
### What is the issue?

Running Tailscale on the host, upgraded to 1.66 this morning. 

Right after the update, my Uptime Kuma Docker container stopped being able to ping my Tailscale IPs. I am able to ping them from the host without a problem, but not from the containers themselves (tried via container console etc). 

Interestingly enough, I can ping the host's Tailscale IP from containers without a problem, but not any other Tailscale IP elsewhere.

What to do?


### Steps to reproduce

_No response_

### Are there any recent changes that introduced the issue?

Upgrade to 1.66

### OS

Linux

### OS version

Ubuntu 22.04.4

### Tailscale version

1.66

### Other software

Docker
Uptime Kuma

### Bug report

BUG-9d84fdefb594944f730cf924acfe7eeb840969eb879e03040299d486a9d800a8-20240509115120Z-6c1d2962b34ab51f

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Saw a similar thing in my setup. Seems to be related to https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/12066

Workaroud (for me): `tailscale up --stateful-filtering=false`

comments.body: Perfect @participant1 that fixed it, thanks so much!

comments.author: participant8
comments.body:
I found another workaround that doesn't require disabling stateful-filtering.

```
sudo iptables -I ts-forward 1 -i docker0 -d 100.64.0.0/10 -j MARK --set-xmark 0x40000/0xff0000
sudo ip6tables -I ts-forward 1 -i docker0 -j MARK --set-xmark 0x40000/0xff0000
```

*Longer explanation:*

Here's the ts-forward chain from nftables (`nft list ruleset`):
```
chain ts-forward {
        iifname "tailscale0" counter packets 0 bytes 0 meta mark set mark and 0xff00ffff xor 0x40000
        meta mark & 0x00ff0000 == 0x00040000 counter packets 0 bytes 0 accept
        oifname "tailscale0" ip saddr 100.64.0.0/10 counter packets 0 bytes 0 drop
        oifname "tailscale0" ct state ! related,established counter packets 550 bytes 46102 drop
        oifname "tailscale0" counter packets 0 bytes 0 accept
}
```

Packets from docker containers on the default docker bridge expect to NAT out to the internet using the docker0 interface as their default gateway. When the containers try to reach a 100.64.0.0/10 carrier-grade NAT IP, routing rules will atempt to send that traffic out the tailscale0 interface. They will match the 4th rule in this chain because they are attempting to route out the tailscale0 interface, and they are not part of a related/established connection state.

The first rule in this chain marks traffic to be accepted only if the incoming interface is tailscale0. The iptables command basically duplicates that mark line in the chain, but it marks any packets coming into the docker0 interface and destined for the carrier-grade NAT address space.

```
sudo iptables -I ts-forward 1 -i docker0 -d 100.64.0.0/10 -j MARK --set-xmark 0x40000/0xff0000
sudo ip6tables -I ts-forward 1 -i docker0 -j MARK --set-xmark 0x40000/0xff0000
```

comments.author: participant8
comments.body:
Another workaround, and maybe this is the actual bug really...

Here's the FORWARD chain from nftables (`nft list ruleset`):
```
chain FORWARD {
        type filter hook forward priority filter; policy drop;
        counter packets 2935 bytes 256404 jump ts-forward
        counter packets 13868 bytes 90667843 jump DOCKER-USER
        counter packets 13868 bytes 90667843 jump DOCKER-ISOLATION-STAGE-1
        oifname "docker0" ct state related,established counter packets 8321 bytes 90336047 accept
        oifname "docker0" counter packets 0 bytes 0 jump DOCKER
        iifname "docker0" oifname != "docker0" counter packets 5544 bytes 330944 accept
        iifname "docker0" oifname "docker0" counter packets 0 bytes 0 accept
}
```

The first rule in there (second line) just jumps all traffic to the `ts-forward` chain. That chain only really handles traffic coming from the tailscale0 interface. Traffic from anywhere else (like docker0) will just get dropped. That rule can be adjusted to only send traffic to ts-forward IF it comes from the tailscale0 interface since it doesn't seem that it's intended to handle traffic from other interfaces. I'm less familiar with how this might work on either exit nodes or nodes that are advertising routes and forwarding traffic to/from other interfaces.

This could be done with:
```
sudo iptables -D FORWARD 1
sudo iptables -I FORWARD 1 -i tailscale0 -j ts-forward
```
This would yield a FORWARD chain like:
```
chain FORWARD {
        type filter hook forward priority filter; policy drop;
        iifname "tailscale0" counter packets 0 bytes 0 jump ts-forward
        counter packets 0 bytes 0 jump DOCKER-USER
        counter packets 13868 bytes 90667843 jump DOCKER-ISOLATION-STAGE-1
        oifname "docker0" ct state related,established counter packets 8321 bytes 90336047 accept
        oifname "docker0" counter packets 0 bytes 0 jump DOCKER
        iifname "docker0" oifname != "docker0" counter packets 5544 bytes 330944 accept
        iifname "docker0" oifname "docker0" counter packets 0 bytes 0 accept
}
```

I didn't bother adjusting the IPv6 rules for this workaround because there are no IPv6 FORWARD rules for docker to interfere with.

comments.author: participant8
comments.body:
> > This could be done with:
> > ```
> > sudo iptables -D FORWARD 1
> > sudo iptables -I FORWARD 1 -i tailscale0 -j ts-forward
> > ```
> 
> is this can fix also host names not reachable?

It sounds like you are conflating too problems at the same time. If you want to resolve MagicDNS names from inside a container, you'll want to be using 100.100.100.100 as your DNS resolver inside the container. That can be done several ways. For example, the docker daemon can default to duplicating your workstation's DNS resolution settings inside the containers.

The problem being discussed in this issue is that your containers won't be able to reach 100.100.100.100 for MagicDNS resolution or any other 100.64/10 addresses for anything else in your tailnet.

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
@participant11 
For problems with DNS resolution from within containers, please see https://github.com/tailscale/tailscale/issues/12108.
For problems with reaching tailnet IPs other than 100.100.100.100 from containers or other LAN hosts, this is the right issue.
And yes, for DNS problems the current recommendation is to use `--stateful-filtering=false` for now. We are thinking about potential fixes or alternatives.

> Same problem here. I'm running Tailscale in a Linux VM on Proxmox (not that the VM or Proxmox should be relevant?) with IP forwarding turned on. My router has a static route for my Tailscale network pointing at the VM so that other devices on my LAN can access my Tailscale network without needing to be nodes themselves. Until I updated to 1.66.1 today this worked fine. Not sure what version I was on before. With 1.66.1 I need to use the --statefule-filtering=false workaround.

@participant10 your setup sounds exactly like the attack we were fixing with stateful filtering and https://tailscale.com/security-bulletins#ts-2024-005 :)
If you understand the risks and wish to keep using this configuration, running with `--steateful-filtering=false` is the way to do it.
